original_question: Determine whether there exists a group G that contains an existential inclusion of F2 such that L(G) is not isomorphic to L(F_n) for some n in N; in particular, determine whether a non-elementary surface group G can satisfy L(G) not isomorphic to L(F_n).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies that the question is a group-level existence problem, that the distinguished subgroup is F_2, that the issue is whether the associated group von Neumann algebra can fail to be isomorphic to a free group factor L(F_n), and that the paper singles out the non-elementary surface-group case as a particularly important special instance.
missing_details: Make explicit that the existentiality is attached to the subgroup inclusion F_2 ≤ Γ in the model-theoretic sense used in the section preamble, not merely to an inclusion of von Neumann algebras.
Define F_n as the free group of rank n and L(Γ) as the group von Neumann algebra of the discrete group Γ.

State the problem as a pure existence question, without adding extra hypotheses not present in the paper (for example icc, separability, Connes embeddability, or inner amenability assumptions are not part of Problem 9).
Keep the paper’s literal quantifier "for some n in N" rather than replacing it with a stronger or different quantifier.
If the question is to be fully stand-alone, clarify what class of groups is meant by "non-elementary surface group," since the paper uses that phrase without a local definition.
refined_question: Does there exist a discrete group Γ containing the rank-two free group F_2 as an existential subgroup such that the group von Neumann algebra L(Γ) is not isomorphic to L(F_n) for some n in N? More specifically, can Γ be taken to be a non-elementary surface group? Here F_n denotes the free group of rank n and L(·) denotes the group von Neumann algebra.
justification: The draft is capturing exactly Problem 9 from the paper’s section "Existential embeddings." In the local setup, the paper first recalls the notion of existential embedding and says that the notion is defined similarly for inclusions of groups; immediately after that, it states the group question with the special surface-group case. The sentence just before Problem 9 also says that this surface-group version is credited to D. Voiculescu. In the nearby context, the paper presents this as a direct open problem rather than giving a separate equivalent reformulation, so the sharpest faithful rewrite is a cleaned-up stand-alone version of Problem 9 itself.
